paper.title: One-week test–retest stability of heart rate variability during rest and deep breathing
paper.claim: Implements a generated methods example for within-person repeatability of selected five-minute resting HRV measures without health interpretation.
paper.population: The paper studied controlled ECG and respiration recordings; the package contains generated participants only.
paper.referenceStandard: Published test-retest method and deterministic participant-grouped generated fixture.
paper.relationEvidence: Independent stdlib ICC(1,1), participant bootstrap, and within-participant coefficient-of-variation example; it does not reproduce the laboratory cohort or acquisition.

compatibility.brainstemContract: brainstem.resting-hrv-methods/v1 plus a proposed distinct-record repeatability selector
requiredSignals: repeated recordings from the same participant
compatibility.window: Two to seven distinct eligible recordings for personal output; exactly seven per participant for cohort reliability.
compatibility.preprocessing: Reuse the reviewed resting-HRV method for heart rate, SDNN, RMSSD, SD1, and SD2; aggregate participants equally; bootstrap participants rather than recordings.
mismatches: Ordinary field recordings do not reproduce the paper's controlled ECG, respiration, posture, acclimation, or time-of-day protocol.
Detector R-R is not asserted to be validated N-N input.
Seven recordings are a bounded product window, not a universal scientific minimum.

cohort.output: Participant-equal aggregate reliability and within-participant variation; no subject or recording rows.

personal.output: Owner-only median, range, and recording-to-recording variation for selected descriptive measures.
